papers.title_en: Shape-Preserving Covariate Adjustment via Empirical Likelihood in Randomized Experiment
papers.authors: Zhilan Lou, Jun Shao, Yuhan Qian, Tuo Wang, Yanyao Yi, Yu Du, Ting Ye
papers.evidence: 随机实验中保留形状的协变量调整方法，可应用于运动对皮瓣存活效果的估计
papers.tldr: 随机实验中协变量调整能提升效率，但传统校准与增广方法在估计分布或生存函数时会破坏单调性等基本形状。本文利用经验似然与协变量平衡约束，为每个处理臂构造协变量调整的经验测度。将各类分布泛函（如分布函数、生存函数、分位数、限制平均生存时间）作为该测度的plug-in估计，自动保持形状，且具有显式保证的效率增益和渐近正态性。所得推断对随机化方案不变，统一了简单随机化与常见协变量自适应设计下的协变量调整与形状保持，模拟与SURPASS-4试验验证了理论优势。
papers.abstract_en: Covariate adjustment improves estimation efficiency in randomized experiments, but standard calibration and augmentation methods, when applied to distribution or survival functions, do not preserve monotonicity---a fundamental property of the estimand. We propose using empirical likelihood with covariate-balancing constraints to construct a covariate-adjusted empirical measure for each treatment arm. Estimators of a broad class of distributional functionals, including cumulative distribution functions, survival functions, quantiles, and restricted mean survival times, are then derived as plug-in functionals of this measure, automatically inheriting proper shape constraints. We establish asymptotic normality with an explicit, guaranteed efficiency gain over unadjusted estimators. The asymptotic distributions are invariant to the randomization scheme, providing a unified inference procedure under simple randomization and all commonly used covariate-adaptive designs satisfying a mild balancing condition. This unified construction, adjusting the empirical measure once and deriving all estimators from it, offers a principled reconciliation of covariate adjustment with shape preservation. Simulations and an application to the SURPASS-4 trial confirm the theoretical gains.
